name: Vantablack Media Chromatic Null Shroud
description:
The Chromatic Null Shroud is a full-body garment woven from Vantablack Media's proprietary photon-harvesting microfiber, capable of absorbing up to 99.96% of incident visible light across a 180-degree arc. Embedded within the weave are micro-actuated chromophore cells that sample ambient light from the environment and dynamically redistribute it across the garment's surface, rendering the wearer as a near-perfect visual void that blends into low-light backgrounds rather than standing out as a silhouette.

What distinguishes the Chromatic Null Shroud from simpler blackout garments is its passive operation mode — it requires no power cell during static concealment, drawing only trace current from body heat via integrated thermoelectric strips. Active dynamic blending, used during slow movement, consumes roughly 0.4W and can be sustained for six hours on a standard micro-cell. The garment's outer layer is also treated with a radar-diffusing aerogel coating that scatters millimeter-wave sensor returns, making it effective against automated perimeter systems.

Originally developed for Vantablack Media's deep-cover documentary crews operating in contested corporate zones, the Shroud quickly found a secondary market among infiltrators, black-bag operatives, and high-end couriers. Its civilian framing as 'broadcast equipment' has kept it in a regulatory gray zone for years, and Vantablack Media has made no apparent effort to close that loophole.

specifications.form_factor: Full-body hooded garment, collapses to 0.4L compression pouch
specifications.thermal_bleed: Minimal — no active suppression, upper body heat still visible to IR

tactical_use: Best deployed in low-light or no-light environments where visual concealment is the primary concern. Users typically pair it with a separate thermal dampener, as the Shroud offers no IR suppression. Effective for slow crawls through monitored corridors, static observation posts, and close-approach surveillance. The compression pouch form factor means it can be worn under a conventional jacket and deployed quickly in the field.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's underground circles, owning a Chromatic Null Shroud is a marker of professional seriousness — it signals that the wearer operates at a level where off-the-shelf dark clothing no longer suffices. Vantablack Media's branding gives it a veneer of journalistic legitimacy that mid-tier operatives exploit shamelessly at checkpoints. Among corporate security analysts, the phrase 'they were wearing the Shroud' has become shorthand for 'we have no visual record of the subject.'
known_users: Vantablack Media field crews in contested broadcast zones
story_hooks: A Chromatic Null Shroud surfaces on the black market still containing trace DNA from a missing Vantablack Media journalist — someone wants it recovered before forensics teams find it.

A rash of corporate espionage incidents all share one detail: security footage shows nothing. The investigating team must determine whether a Shroud was involved or if something far more sophisticated is at work.

Vantablack Media issues a quiet recall on a specific batch of Shrouds, citing 'chromophore degradation.' Operatives who've used those units start receiving unmarked messages suggesting the garments were also collecting biometric data.
A player needs to acquire a Shroud quickly but the only available unit belongs to a Vantablack Media crew currently embedded in a hostile zone — negotiation, theft, or trade required.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting full-body hooded garment that appears as a perfect visual void—the fabric doesn't reflect light so much as *eliminate* it. The weave creates a depth-less silhouette, almost like looking at a humanoid absence rather than a person wearing black. The hood extends to cover the face, with subtle mesh panels at eye level that are imperceptible unless specifically searched for.
physical_description.dimensions: Full-body garment (170–200 cm deployed length); compresses to a 25×20×8 cm pouch when rolled
physical_description.weight_description: 1.1 kg total—light enough to wear for extended periods without fatigue, handheld as a compression bundle
physical_description.primary_material: Proprietary Vantablack Media photon-harvesting microfiber woven with embedded micro-actuated chromophore cells; outer layer treated with radar-diffusing aerogel coating
physical_description.finish: Matte ultra-black with an almost liquid-like visual quality; surface appears to *drink* light rather than reflect it. Subtle iridescent shimmer visible only at oblique angles (chromophore activity indicator). Aerogel coating gives a faint powdery texture appearance in bright direct light, like disturbed carbon dust.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: absolute black (Vantablack™ designation). Accents: faint teal/cyan micro-LED indicators embedded at wrists and along the spine when active mode is engaged. Interior lining is matte charcoal gray.
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimalist: two tactile pressure nodes at left wrist (static/active mode toggle, battery status), micro-USB charging port concealed in right cuff with waterproof cap, thermoelectric strip grid visible as subtle embossed lines along torso and upper legs (body heat harvesting), subtle blue LED indicator in left palm area (passive/active status and power remaining—cycles slowly when inactive, pulses when active)
distinctive_features: The garment appears to have *no reflection*—it absorbs rather than bounces light, creating an unsettling visual void
Micro-actuated chromophore cells create barely-perceptible shimmer patterns when active (dynamic blending mode), like heat haze made solid
Hood design includes reinforced mesh eyeholes that are visually seamless from 1 meter away
Thermoelectric strip grid creates subtle geometric embossing across the weave—functional and aesthetic
Faint aerosol particulate coating on outer surface (radar treatment) creates grainy texture under extreme magnification
Spine-mounted teal status LEDs glow softly when active, creating thin vertical line of light in darkness
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Anchor Broadcasting Platform logo (subtle embossed anchor symbol) on interior left shoulder; discrete serial number laser-etched on charging port cap; regulatory label on inner collar (reads as 'Broadcast Field Equipment — Vantablack Media Division'); warranty barcode on compression pouch
physical_description.condition_typical: Deployed: worn as seamless full-body garment, hood drawn, gloves pulled to wrist, appearing as a human-shaped void in low-light environments. Inactive: color and light-absorption at their peak, completely non-reflective. In use during movement: micro-ripples of teal-cyan light trace across surface as chromophore cells actively sample and redistribute ambient light patterns. Storage: compressed into pouch, surface appears powdery (aerogel coating) until deployed again.

image_prompt: A Vantablack Media Chromatic Null Shroud laid flat on a brushed steel workbench under dramatic workshop lighting. The garment appears as an absolute void—pure black emptiness that seems to swallow light entirely. A single 1-meter soft-key light rakes across the fabric, revealing only the faintest shimmer of its surface texture and the barely-perceptible thermoelectric strip grid. The hood is positioned center-frame, face opening toward camera, revealing nothing but absolute darkness within. The compression pouch sits nearby, its fabric showing powdery aerogel coating in sharp focus. A small status indicator glows soft teal-cyan from the wrist area. Surrounding environment: dimly lit GLMZ workshop—scattered tools, a retro CRT monitor, scattered cable spools. Neo-noir urban aesthetic with cool color grading, dramatic shadows. The garment's impossibly black surface contrasts against matte steel and warm tungsten fixtures. Shallow depth of field emphasizes the fabric's light-eating quality. Shot from 45-degree angle, revealing the garment's form without it appearing flat. --ar 3:2 --v 6
